fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents honestly present a QA-to-DevOps transition and clearly distinguish professional test infrastructure from personal Terraform, monitoring and TLS work. They do not manufacture production cloud ownership, cluster administration, Terragrunt, mTLS or fleet integration. However, the application does little to address the distance between this experience and an independent contractor expected to lead cloud architecture and production delivery.

issues: The two-page length is nominally appropriate, but the entire second page contains only the language section.
The summary omits the supplied overall experience duration and the more useful distinction between QA tenure and infrastructure-focused work.
The technical-skills list could preserve the original Kubernetes proficiency qualifier more explicitly, although the experience section supplies the necessary scope limitation.

reasons: Text extraction is clean, single-column and in sensible reading order.
Cloud and infrastructure wording, TLS, monitoring and CI/CD are present; SSL/TLS is represented by TLS.
Core filters such as Terragrunt and mTLS are absent, and Terraform and AWS are explicitly limited to personal work or learning.
The current and previous titles remain QA-focused, with no professional production-cloud or architecture-leadership role.
Some adjacent concepts are demonstrated indirectly, such as communication through documentation and virtual infrastructure through a VPS, but the corresponding explicit screening terms are absent.

issues: Company tailoring is limited to the advertised fleet-connectivity project; it does not use the supplied engineering-led, end-to-end ownership or collaborative-culture information.
Most of the letter repeats CV achievements rather than explaining the specific contribution the candidate could make within the role's architecture, networking and production scope.
It does not explicitly bridge the substantial seniority and autonomy gap between a career-switch candidate and this contractor engagement.
strengths: Names the correct company and exact role.
Connects the application to the new train fleet and cloud-services project.
Uses strong, supported pipeline-time, runner-cost and flaky-test metrics.
Clearly labels the k3s and Terraform work as personal.
Explicitly credits the platform team with cluster operation.
Does not reuse the earlier letter's outdated employer, learning status or healthcare motivation.

spacing_issues: The CV's second page is only 9.6% filled and contains just the LANGUAGES heading and one line.
The CV's first page is comparatively dense, while almost all of page two is blank; moving the language line or slightly tightening content would avoid the unnecessary page.
issues: The CV's 10-point body text is readable but relatively small for its dense first page.
The letter is clean and readable at 11 points, with reasonable paragraph spacing.
The serif typography is consistent across the documents, but the CV pagination materially reduces the professionalism of the set.

notes_facts_used: AWS EC2 and S3 are learning basics, not professional cloud experience.
Professional Kubernetes access is namespace-level, with the platform team operating the cluster.
Internal CI documentation is used for onboarding.
ISTQB Foundation Level certification obtained in 2019.
CKA study is ongoing and the exam is booked for January 2027, not already passed.
notes_facts_ignored: Explicit junior/mid DevOps or platform target and willingness to accept a junior title.

evaluation.summary: Both documents are accurate, readable and careful about the boundary between professional test infrastructure and personal cloud learning. The strongest evidence is the quantified CI/CD impact, developer support, documentation and clearly scoped Kubernetes work. The application remains a substantial stretch for a contractor expected to lead cloud architecture, strong Terraform/Terragrunt delivery and secure train-to-cloud networking. The main presentation defect is the nearly empty second CV page; the letter is clean but could make a stronger, more specific case for the candidate's realistic contribution.

issues: the last page is only 9.6% filled
